verdict.reasoning: Patient reports waking with a left-sided headache at about 5:30 and that it is still present: "this really horrible pain on the left side of my head" and "it woke me up quite early this morning"; "Probably around 5:30ish"; "Is the headache still present now?" "Yes, it is."
Headache is described as more prominent on the left and different from prior headaches: "this time it's just kind of more prominent on the left side, which I've never really had".

Prior headaches were less severe and across the front (bilateral): "I've had a bit of a history with headaches but nothing as severe as this before" and "normally. They kind of spread across the front of my head."
Patient has mild light sensitivity: "I'm a little bit sensitive. It just, it kind of makes my eyes a little bit sore, but nothing that I can't really handle."
Patient denies neck stiffness, fever, and nausea: "Do you have any neck stiffness at all?" "No."; "do you have any fever?" "No."; "Are you feeling nauseous at all?" "Not really."
Patient reports initial dizziness that resolved: "when I first got up this morning my head felt a bit dizzy, but that's kind of... seems to be fine."
Two-year history of anxiety: "I had, like, anxiety for about two years now and I've been on Sertraline for a while."
Patient denies hypertension: "Have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure?" "No."
When asked about other illnesses, patient says none: "Do you have any other illnesses at all?" "None." Anxiety was already identified separately.
Patient is currently on Sertraline: "I've been on Sertraline for a while." and "Are you taking searching at the moment?" "Yes."

Patient took paracetamol for current headache and it did not help: "In terms of this headache... have you taken anything for it yet?" "I've taken some paracetamol."; "Has that helped?" "Not really, no."
No known drug allergies: "Do you have any allergies to any medication?" "Not that I'm aware of, no."
Mother has anxiety: "My mum's had a history of anxiety as well."

Patient denies family migraines and other physical illness: "Does anyone in your family have any migraines... ?" "No, they haven't." and later "are there any illnesses in your family?" "No, there's nothing. My parents. My mum's had a history of anxiety as well, but no kind of like physical illnesses or anything like that."
Living with partner: "are you living by yourself at the moment or are you living with someone else?" "I live with my partner."
Non-smoker: "Are you a smoker?" "No."

Work stress, backlog, late nights for a couple of months: "Work's kind of a bit stressful... lot of kind of a backlog of work... been doing a lot of late nights as well." and "How long has that been the case for?" "Probably about a couple of months now."
Runs three times per week: "how much exercise would you do normally a week?" "normally I try to go running at least three times a week."
Diet described as okay: "What's your diet like?" "It's okay. It's nothing, nothing really healthy, but it's fine."

Doctor considers tension vs migraine for unilateral headache: "it might be one of two things. It could be an element of what we call tension headache... The other possibility is migraine as well. And the fact what makes that more likely is the fact it's on one side and that you've got some sensitivity to light."

Anxiety present and not currently severe; patient is on Sertraline: "I had, like, anxiety for about two years now and I've been on Sertraline for a while." and "Do you feel anxious at the moment?" "No, not necessarily... Other than that, I don't feel massively anxious." This supports well-controlled anxiety on medication.

Work stress linked to symptoms and addressed in plan: "what makes [tension headache] more likely is the fact that you've been under some pressure and you have a history of anxiety" and the subsequent focus on reducing work stress and time off.

Doctor recommends starting ibuprofen and continuing paracetamol: "the things that we start off first line if someone had migraine would be to start ibuprofen... You can keep on taking paracetamol as well if you like, but the ibuprofen is actually more effective for migraine."
Counseling with self-referral link: "I'd also like you to explore counseling options as well. So there's counseling service in your area that I can give you the link for you to self refer."
Advice about minimizing work stress and taking a week off: "maybe consider taking some time off work... maybe having a week off if you self certify that might help with things."

Hydration and sleep advice: "try and ensure that you're having a minimum of 7, 8 hours sleep at night, every night" and "A minimum of 1.5 to 2 liters of water or fluids a day, and that's not including coffee or tea."

Education on headache danger signs: "I'll also leave a link to some of the danger signs and symptoms of headaches in the notes. If you can read through that... what kind of things should trigger you contacting another doctor."

Follow-up in a week with possible labs/further workup if not better: "we'll have a follow up in a week's time" and "If we're finding that things are not getting better, we might need to arrange some blood tests or look at other possibilities."

Instruction to seek earlier care if worsening/new concerns: "If anything changes in the meantime or you get worried or things get worse, feel free. Have a low threshold for ringing us back and booking an appointment and we can reassess the situation."

No examination or vitals documented; doctor notes limitation: "obviously I haven't been able to examine you or see you directly" and there is no mention of physical exam findings or vital signs in the transcript.
